_schema.memories: Array of { id (stable string), content, category (preference|fact|pattern|decision|outcome), entity, namespace }. The stable id is used only to label queries; Engram assigns its own UUID at insert time and the harness maps between them.
_schema.queries: Array of { id, query (natural-language text), relevant_ids (array of memory ids that SHOULD rank in the top-k) }. Mix direct-fact lookups, paraphrases, and topic queries.
_schema.notes: Several memories are deliberately near-duplicate or topically adjacent (e.g. m01/m34 on Fastify, m10/m38/m39 on pnpm) to stress ranking.

memories.content: Prefers Fastify over Express for Node.js APIs because of its lower overhead and built-in JSON schema validation.
The main API service runs on Node.js 20 using native ESM modules.
The production database is PostgreSQL 15 hosted on AWS RDS.
Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for the billing service because financial transactions need ACID guarantees.
Deploys to production automatically via GitHub Actions on every merge to main.
Runs the full test suite in CI before any deploy; merges are blocked when CI is red.
Migrated the build tooling from Webpack to Vite to cut local dev startup time.
Switching to Vite reduced cold dev-server startup from about 40 seconds to under 3 seconds.
Likes TypeScript for application code but keeps build scripts in plain JavaScript.
Uses pnpm as the package manager across all repos in the monorepo.
Prefers two-space indentation and uses Prettier for automatic formatting.
The frontend is built with React 18 and Tailwind CSS.
Adopted Tailwind CSS to avoid maintaining a bespoke design-system CSS bundle.
Uses short-lived feature branches with squash-merge; there is no long-lived develop branch.
Secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager and never committed to git in a .env file.
Wants error messages to be actionable and to include the offending input value.
Adding request-id tracing cut median incident triage time roughly in half.
Application logs are shipped to CloudWatch as structured JSON.
Standardized on Vitest instead of Jest for faster ESM-native tests.
Writes unit tests for core logic and treats UI tests as manual for the first version.
The team tracks issues in Linear rather than Jira.
Prefers small, frequently shipped pull requests over big-bang releases.
Decided to keep the project zero-dependency at runtime so it stays embeddable.
The command-line interface is built with Commander.js.
Generates typed API clients from the OpenAPI specification during the build.
Caching the embedding model on disk removed the model re-download on every restart.
Embeddings are generated with the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model running locally on CPU.
Chose local CPU embeddings over a hosted embedding API to keep the tool fully offline.
Dislikes making Docker a hard requirement for local development.
Staging and production run in separate AWS accounts.
Rotates database credentials quarterly via an automated job.
Moving session storage to Redis fixed the intermittent logout bug under load.
Redis is used for caching and for rate limiting.
Picked Fastify partly because its plugin system maps cleanly onto the modular services.
Prefers REST over GraphQL for internal service-to-service calls.
The mobile app is built with React Native.
Runs database migrations automatically when a service boots.
Switched from npm to pnpm to speed up CI installs and dedupe the monorepo.
Adopting pnpm cut CI install time from about 90 seconds to 25 seconds.
API rate limiting is set to 100 requests per minute per API key.
Wants documentation kept in the repository as markdown, close to the code.
Every pull request is reviewed by at least one other engineer before merge.
Adopted conventional commits so the changelog can be generated automatically.
Automated changelog generation eliminated the manual release-notes step.
The team is fully remote across three time zones.
Prefers asynchronous written updates over daily standup meetings.
Sentry is used for both frontend and backend error tracking.
Uses Vite's library mode to ship the dashboard as static assets.
Pins exact dependency versions in the lockfile and reviews every dependency bump.
The default API port for the service is 3838.
